text:
Maria Chen: quick follow-up to the offload RFC — we've been seeing long tail pauses when reclaiming pinned GPU pages in dedicated pools. thinking about a "soft shrinker" that only signals eviction candidates and a coordinated background reclaimer that respects workload hints. want thoughts on API boundaries and correctness tradeoffs.
Samir Patel: +1 to separating signal from action. do you mean a per-pool priority queue of candidates, or a global one?
Maria Chen: per-pool makes QoS easier, but global helps avoid thrashing when two pools compete for the same GPU memory. probably hybrid: per-pool queue with global arbitration.
Jordan Lee: what signals are you considering? liveness flags, last-access timestamp, allocation size? also how do we treat pinned IO vs temp KV caches?
Maria Chen: start simple: last_access_ts + allocation_weight (size * cost_factor). pinned IO gets higher eviction cost so lower priority. we can add explicit "do_not_evict" hint for critical DMA buffers.
Priya Nair: how do we expose this to the runtime owners? an opaque hint in the allocator API? eg: alloc(pinned=true, evict_hint="soft") ?
Maria Chen: exactly. prototype API: ``alloc_gpu(size, flags={pinned: true, evict: "soft"})`` and a separate control plane call to register a reclaim callback for a pool. reclaim callback can choose to flush, migrate to CPU, or drop caches.
Samir Patel: worried about complexity for extensions like quantization caches (we prefer to evict quant caches before model weights). can callback see "category" metadata?
Maria Chen: yes include tags: category=model|cache|io and priority int. reclaimer will consult these tags + pool SLAs.
Jordan Lee: locking: if reclaimer migrates a KV cache while an in-flight inference uses it, we need safe handover. do we have a refcounting or migration protocol?
Maria Chen: plan is refcounts + NONBLOCKING migrate op. sequence: mark candidate -> attempt migrate (steal page) -> if refcount>0, fall back to copy-on-read (move to CPU copy) -> update page table. fallbacks increase latency but avoid correctness issues.
Priya Nair: metrics we should add: time-to-evict, evictions-per-second, failed-evicts, and "evict-induced-latency" per route. want dashboards before rollout.
Samir Patel: agree. also need a safety valve: global soft-threshold that refuses soft-evictions when p99 latency > SLO.
Maria Chen: good call. add a governor that watches serve latency and temporarily throttles reclaim aggressiveness.
Jordan Lee: can we experiment with different cost_factors? I ran a small sim where cost_factor=1 for weights, 0.2 for caches — reduced regens by 35% but increased mean memory by 8%.
Maria Chen: nice. please drop sim and config in #eng-runtime-experiments. we should also try a version where pinned buffers are allowed brief grace windows (200-500ms) before becoming evictable.
Priya Nair: question on rollout: feature flag per-cluster + canary on low-traffic customer. also need docs for "do_not_evict" semantics.
Maria Chen: rollout plan: feature flag -> canary 1% -> 10% -> 50%. default off for Dedicated until we validate. I'll draft RFC follow-up with pseudocode and metrics.
reclaim-bot: background reclaim job scheduled for pool gpu-cluster-7 (candidates: 42)
Samir Patel: thanks — lgtm. next step: Maria, can you add the API sketch and the sim results to the RFC thread?
Maria Chen: will do, thanks for the feedback :+1:
